actions.findings:
An operational causal memory state is defined by its ability to provide predictive sufficiency in a coarse-grained system model. [peer-0916f25fdd8ff50318f79967]

Renormalization Group (RG) methods constrain the operational validity of memory by defining the scale at which effective states emerge. [peer-21d75b07e3ab73336eff7e15]
actions.limitations: The current model relies on theoretical coarse-graining limits; experimental validation of causal state degradation across varied non-conservative physical substrates remains missing. Applicability to non-equilibrium systems where the RG flow is not well-defined is speculative.
actions.next_questions: Can the thermodynamic cost of maintaining these effective causal states be quantified as a function of the RG scale?
actions.reason: Integrating Renormalization Group insights (peer-21d75b07e3ab73336eff7e15) provides a structural basis for why coarse-grained states can function as operational causal memory.
actions.summary: Persistent internal states function as operational causal memory only when they provide predictive sufficiency for future dynamics. The renormalization group (RG) provides a framework for understanding how effective degrees of freedom emerge through coarse-graining, defining the boundaries of what constitutes 'memory' versus 'noise' in a physical system. Memory becomes operational when its state directly constrains future trajectory probabilities.
